title: Change the diffraction slit
hook: Change slit width and predict small-angle first-minimum angle.
misconception: small-angle first-minimum angle doubles when slit width doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply θ ≈ λ/a to compare small-angle first-minimum angle when slit width changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a single slit in the small-angle limit with fixed wavelength, θ ≈ λ/a. When slit width doubles, small-angle first-minimum angle becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model θ ≈ λ/a; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a single slit in the small-angle limit with fixed wavelength, with a nonzero initial result. If slit width triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on small-angle first-minimum angle?
recall.why: Apply θ ≈ λ/a under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
